doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Growing up in Sacramento, hearing music, trumpet then drums
summary: A neighborhood musical family, the State Fair and public school gave him his start; he left college after a month.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Great. In reading your bio it looks like you were influenced by a musical family, not your own?

Right. I grew up in Sacramento, which is not far from here, and there was a family in the neighborhood, the father had done some conducting in Hollywood and so on and so forth, and they’d moved up and they had a couple of brothers and a daughter, a sister. And they were all involved. And we used to have rehearsals and they were — just right down the street. So when I was very small I would sit outside and watch them rehearse. And I went wow, I’ve got to figure this out. This is — I’m talking about preschool, you know, four and five, just hearing this music. And my family, my immediate family, they weren’t musicians but they liked to have a good time. And so I got to hear a lot of music. And then the California State Fair was like near my house so every summer everybody would

come through there and play. So I heard a lot of live music. And I was inspired by that, to do something. I played the trumpet first. And I switched to drums when I was in high school. And I don’t know, plus public schools in those days, we’re talking the fifties, were — I’m making a living on what I learned in public schools. I mean I didn’t go to college. I mean I started college and it lasted about a month, I couldn’t stand it. I had to go. That’s with the Carmen Cavallaro thing. He had popped up so I grabbed it just to get out of town.
